opts: 2 to 4 weeks before the gestation of the previous adverse outcome
At 37 completed weeks of gestation, whatever the prior outcome
From the day the pregnancy test first becomes positive
Only once labour contractions have begun spontaneously
exp: After an unexplained stillbirth, antepartum fetal surveillance should begin 2 to 4 weeks prior to the gestational age at which the previous adverse outcome occurred.

opts: Lightening, or the welcome sign, from engagement of the head
Uteroplacental insufficiency with a falling fundal height
Pathological oligohydramnios with reduced fetal growth
Arrest of engagement with a persistently floating head
exp: When the fundal height at 40 weeks matches that at 32 weeks, the phenomenon is lightening ('welcome sign'), due to engagement of the fetal head.

opts: To confirm uterine size and whether it is anteverted or retroverted
To diagnose fetal anaemia before the evacuation begins
To determine the maternal Rh antigen type on the spot
To measure serum bile acids from a swab taken at the os
exp: Before suction evacuation a P/V examination in lithotomy confirms uterine size and position, whether anteverted or retroverted.

opts: Spiegelberg criteria for ovarian pregnancy
Studdiford criteria for abdominal pregnancy
Swansea criteria for acute fatty liver of pregnancy
Paalman criteria; Rubin criteria are obsolete
exp: Cervical ectopic pregnancy is diagnosed on Paalman criteria; the Rubin criteria are obsolete.

opts: Methylergometrine, since it contracts the uterus and traps the second twin
Oxytocin, since it causes maternal hypotension at this stage
Misoprostol, since it causes pyrexia at this stage of labour
Magnesium sulfate, since it causes maternal sedation and drowsiness
exp: After delivery of the first twin, methylergometrine is contraindicated because it causes uterine contractions that trap the second twin.

opts: Rh positivity of the fetus alone, without any other factor
Female sex of the fetus alone, without any other factor
Fetal weight above 3 kg alone, without any other factor
Substantial risk of physical or mental abnormalities in the fetus
exp: The listed fetal indication for MTP is a substantial risk of physical or mental abnormalities in the fetus.

opts: Consent, adequate analgesia by epidural or pudendal block, and episiotomy
General anaesthesia, which is mandatory for all forceps deliveries
An oxytocin bolus given immediately before the blades are applied
A urinary catheter left in situ throughout the whole procedure
exp: Prior to forceps delivery one must obtain consent, give adequate analgesia (epidural or pudendal block) and perform an episiotomy.

opts: Preterm labour or premature rupture of the membranes
Normal fetal movements with a reassuring cardiotocograph
Mild nausea in the second trimester of the pregnancy
Rh negativity of the mother with no evidence of sensitisation
exp: A vaginal cerclage may be removed earlier than 37 weeks if preterm labour or premature rupture of membranes supervenes.

opts: A cervical T shape on the transvaginal scan
A complex adnexal mass from areas of haemorrhage
An intrauterine yolk sac seen within the cavity
The Buddha sign of a collapsed empty sac
exp: The most common inconclusive TVS finding in ectopic pregnancy is a complex adnexal mass due to areas of hemorrhage.

opts: Intercourse, physical exercise, heavy lifting and standing 4 hours or more
All household work and walking about inside the house
Normal oral fluid intake and normal dietary salt intake
Transvaginal scans, which must be avoided after 28 weeks
exp: With a low-lying placenta the patient is advised to avoid intercourse, physical exercise, heavy lifting and standing for 4 hours or more.

opts: Clinical pelvimetry; routine pelvimetry is not recommended
X-ray pelvimetry, which should be done routinely
Magnetic resonance imaging pelvimetry done routinely
External pelvimetry alone, with no internal assessment
exp: The best method of diagnosing a contracted pelvis is clinical pelvimetry; routine pelvimetry is not recommended.

opts: False – CPD applies to the current fetus only, so it is not an indication
True – a repeat caesarean section should always be performed next time
True – but only when the disproportion was severe in this labour
False – but it means induction of labour is needed next time
exp: False: CPD is relative to the current fetus only and is not an indication for recurrent caesarean section.

opts: Twin above singleton; monochorionic above dichorionic; heart defects
Singleton above twin; dichorionic above monochorionic
Dichorionic above monochorionic; neural tube defects only
Twin above singleton; monochorionic above dichorionic; renal defects
exp: Congenital anomalies are commoner in twins than singletons, commoner in monochorionic than dichorionic twins, and heart defects predominate.

opts: Uterine hyperstimulation or tachysystole from oxytocin or misoprostol
Administration of prophylactic ampicillin during the induction
Artificial rupture of membranes performed to augment labour
Maternal oral hydration with plain water throughout the labour
exp: The most frequent iatrogenic cause of acute prolonged decelerations in induced labour is uterine hyperstimulation (tachysystole) from oxytocin or misoprostol.

opts: Low-dose aspirin 80-150 mg/day started before 16 weeks, ideally 12
High-dose aspirin 300 mg/day started after 28 weeks
Calcium supplementation only, started after 20 weeks
Low-molecular-weight heparin from the time of conception
exp: PIH prophylaxis in twin pregnancy uses low-dose aspirin 80-150 mg/day started before 16 weeks, ideally at 12 weeks.

opts: A possible small increased risk of oral clefts, lip or palate
A high incidence of neural tube defects in the fetus
Induction of fetal renal agenesis in the first trimester
A definite risk of phocomelia after first-trimester use
exp: Ondansetron is generally avoided during early organogenesis (under 10 weeks) because of a possible association with a small increased risk of oral clefts (cleft lip or palate).

opts: Perineural edema, hypercoagulability and physiological immunosuppression
Direct herpes zoster encephalitis involving the facial nucleus
Compression by an intracranial aneurysm of the posterior circulation
Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis occurring late in the third trimester
exp: Bell's palsy in the third trimester is attributed mainly to perineural edema, hypercoagulability and physiological immunosuppression.

opts: To treat asymptomatic bacteriuria found in the pregnant woman
To prevent the onset of normal spontaneous labour at term
To save the woman's life or prevent grave physical or mental injury
To ensure the fetus reaches macrosomia before the delivery
exp: The listed health-based indication for MTP is to save the pregnant woman's life or to prevent grave physical or mental injury.

opts: Higher fetal loss, talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) and amniotic fluid leakage
Amniocytes cannot be karyotyped before 15 weeks of gestation
The fetal heart is arrested by the needle puncture in every case
Amniotic fluid is devoid of alpha-fetoprotein before 15 weeks
exp: Early amniocentesis before 15 weeks is not recommended because of significantly higher fetal loss rates, talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) and fluid leakage.

opts: Elevated blood pressure alone, above 140/90 mmHg
A history of a prior pregnancy affected by hypertension
Proteinuria and/or signs of maternal end-organ damage
Onset of the hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation
exp: In the source comparison, proteinuria and/or signs of end-organ damage distinguish pre-eclampsia from gestational hypertension.

opts: Third trimester, and it may appear within 48 hours after delivery
Only before 12 weeks of gestation in early pregnancy
Only after 12 weeks following delivery in the puerperium
Only during labour presenting before 20 weeks of gestation
exp: HELLP commonly presents in the third trimester, and it may also be seen within 48 hours after delivery.

opts: DCDA (dizygotic); among monozygotic, MCDA
MCDA overall; among monozygotic, DCDA
MCMA overall; among monozygotic, DCDA
DCDA overall; among monozygotic, MCMA
exp: The commonest variety of twins overall is DCDA (dizygotic), and among monozygotic twins it is MCDA.

opts: Instrumental delivery; vulval from the internal pudendal artery, vaginal from the vaginal artery
Spontaneous labour; the bleeding comes from the uterine artery
Precipitate labour; the bleeding comes from the ovarian artery
Episiotomy; the bleeding comes from the inferior rectal artery
exp: Vulval hematoma follows instrumental delivery (the commonest cause); vulval hematomas come from the internal pudendal artery and vaginal ones from the vaginal artery.

opts: Raises intracellular calcium and decidual PGF2α; t½ 3-5 min; onset 3 min
Lowers intracellular calcium; t½ 40 min; onset 10 min
Raises cyclic AMP in the myometrium; t½ 1 h; onset 1 min
Blocks progesterone receptors; t½ 20 min; onset 5 min
exp: IM oxytocin raises intracellular calcium and decidual PGF2α; half-life 3-5 minutes, onset 3 minutes, duration 1 hour, and it causes after-pains and milk ejection.

opts: Head seen at the labia irrespective of contractions, episiotomy only if needed
Head visible at the labia only during a contraction
Descent of the head down onto the pelvic levator ani muscle
Delivery of the head by extension over the stretched perineum
exp: Crowning is the head seen at the labia irrespective of contractions, with episiotomy only if required.

opts: Hepatosplenomegaly and bone-marrow hyperplasia increasing erythrocytes
Reduced erythropoiesis within the fetal bone marrow and liver
Fetal insulin suppression from maternal antibody transfer
Maternal platelet activation with consumptive coagulopathy
exp: Erythroblastosis fetalis reflects the compensatory response of hepatosplenomegaly and bone-marrow hyperplasia producing more erythrocytes.

opts: Falling estrogen reduces myometrial contractility, so labour is hard to start
Rising estrogen makes the labour precipitate and very short
Rising progesterone causes uterine rupture before labour
Falling prostaglandins alone, with normal estrogen levels
exp: Post-term pregnancy is explained by reduced estrogen leading to reduced myometrial contractility, so initiating labour is difficult.

opts: Moderate or severe: caesarean; mild: a trial of labour
All degrees: caesarean section without a trial
All degrees: a trial of labour aiming for vaginal delivery
Mild: caesarean section; severe: a trial of labour
exp: For CPD at the inlet, moderate or severe disproportion needs caesarean section, while mild disproportion allows a trial of labour.

opts: Leukocytosis up to 15,000/mcL in pregnancy and 25,000/mcL in labour, with mild thrombocytopenia
Severe leukopenia with a marked reactive thrombocytosis in pregnancy
Pancytopenia affecting all cell lines across every trimester
Marked basophilia with severe thrombocytopenia below 50,000/mcL
exp: Normal pregnancy shows leukocytosis (up to 15,000/mcL, or 25,000/mcL in labor) and mild gestational thrombocytopenia, with the count still at or above 100,000/mcL.

opts: Neonatal sepsis occurring in the first week of life
Asymptomatic bacteriuria, candidiasis and puerperal sepsis
Rubella, measles and mumps acquired during pregnancy
Urinary tuberculosis affecting the renal tract only
exp: Infections listed as increased in diabetes in pregnancy are asymptomatic bacteriuria, candidiasis and puerperal sepsis.

opts: Elective caesarean at 34-35 weeks and 6/7 days, then hysterectomy with placenta in situ
Elective caesarean at 39 completed weeks, then removal of the placenta
Vaginal delivery followed by manual removal of the placenta at delivery
Methotrexate therapy, then curettage once the placenta separates
exp: ACOG's management of choice for antenatally detected PAS is elective caesarean at 34-35 weeks and 6/7 days, followed by hysterectomy with the placenta left in situ.

opts: Ovarian vein, right more than left; cord-like structure; culture negative; MRI or CT
Uterine vein; a fluctuant mass on palpation; culture positive; ultrasound
Iliac artery; a pulsatile mass on palpation; culture positive; Doppler
Renal vein; nothing palpable on examination; culture negative; plain X-ray
exp: Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis affects the ovarian vein (right more than left), shows a cord-like structure on P/V, has a negative blood culture because the infection is localized, and MRI or CT may show the thrombosed vein.

opts: Fundus into the cavity not beyond the os : fundus at the os : fundus outside the introitus : complete inversion
Dimple in the fundus : fundus at the os : fundus in the vagina : fundus outside
Fundus at the os : fundus in the vagina : fundus at the introitus : vagina everted
Fundus in the vagina : at the introitus : outside : with the bladder drawn in
exp: By extent, inversion is graded: 1st the fundus dips into the cavity but not beyond the os; 2nd it reaches the os without protruding; 3rd it protrudes out of the introitus; 4th there is complete inversion of uterus and vagina.

opts: Only at 20 and 22 completed weeks of gestation
At 28-30 and 34-36 weeks, with at least a 3-week gap
Only once, at 12 completed weeks of gestation
Daily scans from 32 completed weeks until delivery
exp: The listed growth-scan schedule for pregestational diabetes is at 28-30 and 34-36 weeks, with at least a 3-week gap.

opts: Cerclage plus progesterone support
Low-dose aspirin on its own
No treatment is given at all
Methotrexate to end the pregnancy
exp: After one prior painless second-trimester loss or early preterm labour, a cervical length under 2.5 cm at 14 weeks is managed with cerclage plus progesterone.

opts: Vascular villi with less hydropic change in partial; avascular villi with extensive change in complete
Avascular villi in the partial mole; vascular villi in the complete mole
Villi are absent in both partial and complete molar pregnancies
Fetal tissue is absent in the partial mole but present in the complete mole
exp: On HPE, the gold standard, partial mole shows vascular villi with less hydropic change, while complete mole shows avascular villi with extensive hydropic degeneration.

opts: Maternal vitals, fetal heart sounds and bleeding, with blood arranged
Only a weekly serum beta-hCG measurement is required
Cervical length measured every single day by ultrasound
Serial magnetic resonance imaging of the pelvis each week
exp: Monitoring during expectant management covers maternal vitals, fetal heart sounds and bleeding, with blood arranged in advance.

opts: Caesarean preferred, though vaginal delivery can be done
Mandatory caesarean section in absolutely every single case
Mandatory vaginal delivery, caesarean is never considered
Forceps delivery to shorten the second stage of the labour
exp: A low-lying placenta 1-2 cm from the internal os is best managed by caesarean section, though vaginal delivery can be done.

opts: Not fixed; fixed; it infers fixation and descent of the head
Fixed; not fixed; it infers the attitude of the head
Engaged; floating; it infers the lie of the fetus in utero
Deflexed; flexed; it infers the position of the fetal head
exp: In the Pawlik grip, a ballotable head means it is not fixed and a non-ballotable head means it is fixed; the grip infers fixation, that is descent of the head into the pelvis.

opts: Inward scalloping and concavity of the frontal calvarial bones
A narrow, elongated anterior fontanelle seen on the scan
Widening of the cisterna magna in the posterior fossa
Bulging parietal bones with premature coronal synostosis
exp: The lemon sign is inward scalloping and concavity of the frontal calvarial bones, due to reduced intracranial pressure.

opts: Loss of the neuronal membrane potential in the cerebral cortex
Reduced cerebral edema and oxidative stress, with membrane stabilisation
Increased cerebral edema, which lowers the seizure threshold
Increased free-radical production within the cerebral cortex
exp: MgSO4 protects the brain in eclampsia by reducing cerebral edema and oxidative stress and by stabilising membranes.

opts: Immediate cervical cerclage before the woman leaves
Immediate laparotomy to exclude an ectopic gestation
No Rh-related consideration is needed at all after this event
Reassurance and anti-D if Rh-positive exposure requires it
exp: After complete abortion the listed management is reassurance and anti-D if Rh-positive exposure requires it.

opts: -5 at the inlet, +5 at the outlet, and 0 at the ischial spines
0 at the inlet, +5 at the outlet, and -5 at the ischial spines
-3 at the inlet and +3 at the outlet, 0 at the ischial spines
-5 at the inlet and 0 at the outlet, -3 at the ischial spines
exp: On the station scale from inlet to outlet, the inlet is -5, the outlet is +5, and 0 is at the ischial spines.

opts: Tip of the coccyx, ischial tuberosities; AP 13 cm; transverse bituberous 11 cm
Sacral promontory, ischial spines; AP 11 cm; transverse 13 cm
Tip of the coccyx, ischial spines; AP 10 cm; transverse 10 cm
Ischial spines, ischial tuberosities; AP 12 cm; transverse 12 cm
exp: The pelvic outlet is bounded posteriorly by the tip of the coccyx and laterally by the ischial tuberosities; its AP diameter is 13 cm and its transverse (bituberous) diameter is 11 cm.
